papers.headline: Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae
papers.summary: We present early-time optical photometry and spectroscopy for a sample 27 previously unpublished type II supernovae (SNe II) observed by the Precision Observations of Infant Supernova Explosions (POISE) collaboration, combined with a literature sample of 59 events to form a total sample of 86 objects.
papers.title: Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae

papers.headline: Entering the Era of Circumplanetary Ring Detection with Direct Imaging
papers.summary: Rings are ubiquitous among the giant planets in the Solar System, yet their presence around exoplanets remains observationally unconstrained.
papers.title: Entering the Era of Circumplanetary Ring Detection with Direct Imaging

papers.headline: Revisiting the Mass and Scale Dependence of the "Lensing is Low" Effect with DECADE
papers.summary: Galaxy-galaxy lensing (GGL) is a critical probe of cosmology and galaxy formation. However, predicted GGL amplitudes tend to be ∼ 20-40% higher than observations, primarily on small scales, a tension called the lensing-is-low problem.
papers.title: Revisiting the Mass and Scale Dependence of the "Lensing is Low" Effect with DECADE
papers.authors: K. Queen, A. V. Fisher, J. U. Lange
